title: Per-token scheduler saturation and cache coherence proforma
body:
Overview:

Quick working notes on an observed class of tail-latency spikes when running mixed-model workloads (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B) with MoE routing enabled and long-context requests (>16k tokens). This doc collects traces, hypotheses, lightweight repro steps, and a mitigation checklist to triage scheduler saturation vs. cache coherence interactions. Purpose is to capture reproducible artifacts and next actions for follow-up experiments.

Motivation / symptoms observed:
- Burst tail latency (p99.9) increases by 2-4x for sequences past ~12k tokens under mixed traffic.
- Latency spikes correlate with low GPU utilization periods and sudden increase in CPU-side scheduling waits.
- MoE requests (gating + multi-expert fanout) amplify the phenomenon; single-model baseline without MoE shows milder effect.
- KV-cache hit rate dips in tandem with scheduler stalls (observed in sampling window).

Short hypothesis summary:
1) Per-token request scheduler is saturating on CPU thread pool during expert fanout and KV serialization, causing token emission stalls despite GPU being nominally free (idle kernel gaps).
2) When KV-cache evictions or delta-KV compressions occur for long-context, workers block on cache coherency (locks / mmap page faults), increasing time between token steps and widening tail.
3) Model-specific routing shapes: Llama's dense attention memory patterns stress PCIe/NUMA differently than Qwen/Mistral which are more bandwidth-friendly; combined with MoE gating, this leads to misaligned prefetch windows and scheduler hot loops.

Experiment setup (baseline repro):
- Hardware: 8x A100 80GB (NVLink) in a 2-socket host. Single NUMA domain per GPU group.
- Software: runtime-main@release-2024-09-rc3 + perf hooks, scheduler-threadpool V2.
- Models: llama-2-13b (dense), mistral-7b (dense), qwen-7b (dense), custom-moe-7b (2-expert topk).
- Workload: interleaved requests: 60% long-context chat (start: 1k, then append to 16k), 40% short generative queries. Concurrent QPS: 80.
- Tracing: per-token traces (timing: token_enter, token_schedule_enqueue, token_worker_start, token_gpu_launch, token_gpu_done, token_emit). Kernel-level perf, nvprof slices for kernel gaps.

Representative trace excerpt (abridged):
- token 1234: enter=0.000, enqueue=0.001, worker_start=0.0012, gpu_launch=0.0013, gpu_done=0.0071, emit=0.0072
- token 1235: enter=0.0073, enqueue=0.0073, worker_start=0.0166, gpu_launch=0.0167, gpu_done=0.0229, emit=0.02295
- token 1236: enter=0.0230, enqueue=0.0230, worker_start=0.0232, gpu_launch=0.0233, gpu_done=0.0239, emit=0.02395
Observations: a 9ms gap between worker_start for token 1235 and prior token emit. Gaps often align with scheduler_enqueue->worker_start delta.

CPU-side counters (sampled during spike window):
- scheduler.queue_wait_ms (median): 0.5ms
- scheduler.queue_wait_ms (p99.9): 14.7ms
- kv_cache.lock_wait_ms (p99.9): 8.9ms
- cpu_context_switches/sec: +28%
- gpu_utilization: 42% (drops to 10% briefly at spike peaks)

KV-cache signals:
- delta-kv compression enabled: yes (adaptive thresholding).
- observed compression GC runs coincide with p99.9 scheduler waits.
- cache hit-rate: 0.87 baseline, dips to 0.62 during spikes.

Model-architecture notes (what differs and why it matters):
- Llama: longer kv-states per token (bigger activations) -> eviction cost higher; prefetch windows must be larger to avoid page faults.
- Mistral: smaller per-token memory, but attention kernel splits more often -> more frequent kernel launches with smaller runtime, making scheduler overhead proportionally more relevant.
- Qwen: more aggressive rotary and packed-query layout -> memory patterns are denser and cause fewer small-page faults but higher contiguous bandwidth needs.
- MoE: expert fanout creates many small GPU jobs that must be serialized or coalesced by scheduler; gating cost runs on CPU and increases the scheduling pressure.

Initial root-cause triangulation:
- The critical path is not purely GPU compute; gaps in GPU kernel timeline line up with CPU scheduling waits and occasional page-fault/reload cycles for KV-sharded memory.
- When MoE is active, CPU gating and preparing scatter/gather indices increases enqueue bursts causing thread-pool queueing.
- Long-context increases KV working set; when combined with delta compression, a compression pass or eviction creates synchronous locks that block workers handling new tokens.

Low-effort repro to iterate locally:
1) Start runtime with --threadpool-size=48 --kv-compression=adaptive --scheduler-mode=default
2) Run workload generator script: workload/mix_long_append.py --qps 80 --moe 0.6 --append-rate 1k/10s
3) Collect traces: curl http://localhost:8080/trace/start; run for 5 minutes; curl http://localhost:8080/trace/stop
4) Post-process: tools/trace-agg.py --window 100ms --emit p99.9,summaries > /tmp/trace-summary.txt

Quick mitigation checklist (ordered by expected effort):
- Fast (config change): reduce scheduler threadpool contention by moving gating off main worker threads: --gating-executor=dedicated. Try enabling prefetching for KV: --kv-prefetch=on --kv-prefetch-window=4k.
- Medium: change scheduler policy to favor FIFO per-session to reduce interleaving churn: --scheduler-policy=session-affinity. Increase background compression window to avoid synchronous GC during bursts.
- Heavy: redesign KV lock granularity (shard-level rather than global) and move compression to async background thread with bounded backlog. Coalesce MoE expert scatter-gather into single fused kernel per token where possible.

Small experimental results (quick A/B runs):
- Baseline (no gating-executor): p99.9 = 138ms, cache-hit median 0.87
- gating-executor=dedicated: p99.9 = 54ms, cache-hit median 0.86
- gating-executor=dedicated + kv-prefetch-window=4k: p99.9 = 28ms, cache-hit median 0.92
- scheduler-policy=session-affinity: p99.9 = 22ms, observed smoother per-token latencies but increased average latency by 6% under heavy short-query burst.

Risks / tradeoffs noted:
- Increasing prefetch window increases memory pressure -> potential OOM if many simultaneous long-context sessions. Need dynamic adaptive window per-customer.
- Session-affinity can harm throughput when many small independent queries starve slots; requires quota/capacity adjustments.
- Async compression backlog needs throttling to control tail if backlog grows unbounded.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we measure mmap page-faults more precisely and correlate to specific eviction calls? (action: add perf probe on madvise/mremap/unmap events).
- Does changing delta-kv compression to heuristic-driven (based on recent token variance) reduce synchronous GC? (action: experiment branch: feature/kv-compress-heuristic).
- For MoE: evaluate fused expert-kernel approach on Qwen vs Llama shapes; which model benefits more from coalesced kernels? (action: microbench PR#321).
- Can we expose per-session prefetch windows via API to avoid global settings?

Immediate next actions (owner / ETA):
- Evelyn Chen -> Add perf probe for page-faults and scheduler queue depth (ETA: 3 days).
- Marco Ruiz -> Prototype gating-executor change in staging and run 24h soak (ETA: 1 week).
- Aisha Patel -> Implement kv-prefetch-window tuning knob and run memory-safety sweep (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Jonah Li -> Bench fused-expert-kernel feasibility on 2 GPUs (ETA: 2 weeks).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider back-pressure signal propagation to client: if scheduler queue depth > X, respond with lighter token window to avoid pushing more long-context writes.
- For customers on Dedicated, expose a toggle for conservative kv-eviction to prevent long-tail when customers stitch huge contexts.
- Keep a small synthetic test harness that mimics mixed-model MoE gating + long-append since production pattern is what triggers this.

Attachments / artifacts stored:
- /artifacts/trace/2024-10-03-long-append-0800.trace (raw)
- /artifacts/perf/2024-10-03-scheduler-hotspots.txt
- PR: github repo/infra/PR#321 (fused expert kernel experiment)

Slack refs: #serving-runtime perf thread (ts: 1700001234)

End of doc.

(Quick editorial: this is intentionally a working note - will formalize into a runbook once gating-executor + kv-prefetch prove stable across models.)
